A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAIL research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments across 18 tasks, baseline comparisons, module ablations, training-mixture experiments, attention visualizations, and cross-task generalization results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including Figures 4–6, Tables 1–2, and the attention, transfer, and distillation comparisons.

M1.justification: TAIL retains Linear Transition, Atomic State, and Memory Fetcher, implemented through program-synthesized CoT and supervised fine-tuning. The new motivation appendix explains these existing components without changing their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 18 tasks across eight algorithm classes, with the same arithmetic variants and cross-task scenarios. v3 Table C1 corresponds to v2 Table B1; relocated plots introduce no additional coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Qwen2.5-7B Base and Instruct, DeepSeek-R1, Index Hint, Reversed Format, and R1-Distill-Qwen2.5-7B. The additional related-work citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 retains the training budget, batch size, learning rates, zero-shot greedy pass@1 evaluation, and two-model grading procedure. Length ranges, sample counts, and training-mixture configurations also match. No revised experimental design is described.

E4.justification: Module and style ablations, training-mixture sensitivity, attention visualizations, cross-task transfer, and the Word Flip case study are retained. v2 Figure D1 becomes v3 Figure 6; this is relocation and redesign of the existing analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Their point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Matching tables and plotted values are unchanged, including all benchmark, style-ablation, and training-mixture panels. Table 1 retains TAIL accuracies of 97.0, 92.5, and 86.5. The token-use, distillation, attention, and cross-task results are also retained.

T1.justification: The Turing-machine definitions, transition equation, and CoT correspondence in Section 2 and Appendix A are unchanged. New Appendix B provides conceptual motivation, without adding mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about TAIL's three components, applicability to computable problems, length generalization, superiority to the reported baselines, and the limited importance of linguistic thinking style.

C2.justification: Appendix B consolidates the existing shortcut-reasoning and attention-localization explanations. v3 Section 6 reproduces v2 Appendix L's limitations concerning cross-task transfer, closed-source models, and non-deterministic or open-ended reasoning. These are clarified or relocated rather than substantively revised interpretations.

D1.justification: The synthesis instructions, query-template information, baseline formatting examples, hyperparameters, and evaluation-model details are retained. v3 adds no implementation procedure or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds an extensive 'Eliciting Chain-of-Thought' discussion covering prompting, SFT, and RL, with newly cited works including ReAct, CoT Collection, Satori, and EvoCoT. This substantially broadens the positioning of program-generated TAIL traces relative to model-generated reasoning.

P1.justification: v3 adds a compact motivation appendix and a related-work paragraph, moves the detailed limitations into Section 6, and makes localized wording and emphasis edits. The main section order and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, the benchmark and mixture plots are extensively reformatted, and Table 2 is split into readable stacked blocks. The Memory Fetcher diagram and mixture plot move into the main text. v3 Figure 4 also introduces a '675B' legend inconsistent with the retained '671B' text.

improvement.justification: The motivation summary and broader related-work discussion improve clarity and context. Moving supporting figures into the main text and enlarging Table 2 make existing evidence easier to access. These limited gains outweigh the denser benchmark plots and inconsistent model-size legend; the scientific method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
